title: Why you sometimes wake up and can't move 😨
subject: sleep
description:
Has this ever happened to you? 👇

Why do you sometimes wake up and can't move? It's called sleep paralysis: during REM (dream) sleep your brain relaxes your muscles so you don't act out your dreams, and sometimes you wake up before that switch turns off. Episodes usually last seconds to a couple of minutes and aren't physically dangerous; if it happens often or disturbs your sleep, talk to a doctor.

Sources: Cleveland Clinic ("Sleep Paralysis")
tags: why can't i move when i wake up

scenes.text: You wake up, but you can't move.
Your eyes open and you can breathe, but your arms and legs won't move.
Some people feel pressure on their chest or sense someone in the room.
But here's the strange part. Your body is doing exactly what it's supposed to do.
In dream sleep, your brain switches off your muscles so you don't act out your dreams.
Sleep paralysis is waking up before that switch turns back on. It usually ends within a couple of minutes.
